samples.summary: Top-level design doc still documents the old `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` default (shadow) after the flip to enforce-by-default
samples.evidence: `docs/design/sharing.md:208-219`: "This is **off by default**. `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` is unset in a stock deployment, which puts the controller in shadow mode: it logs the decision it would have made and answers `allowed: true` anyway… in the default one the client-side `readOnly` flag is the write boundary". After `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (`packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:20`) unset means *enforce*, so this doc now describes the inverse of the shipped behaviour — and it is the doc the new notes wrapper and `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts` both point readers at. Same stale claim at `docs/design/template-gallery.md:668` ("with `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE` unset the auth webhook only *shadows*"). Both are top-level design docs, so only their backticked paths are CI-checked, not their prose.

samples.summary: The docs package's read-only wrapper (and its editor) still assert the webhook "ships in shadow mode by default" — the same claim this change corrected in the notes copy
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:38-42`: "the Yorkie auth webhook — ships in shadow mode by default (`YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE`), so with the default configuration this flag is the write boundary". Same in `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4411-4415` ("ships in shadow mode unless `YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true`, so in a stock deployment this is the write boundary"). The new `packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:57-70` explicitly retracts that framing for notes; the docs package, the other consumer of the same env contract, was left describing the pre-change default. No behaviour breaks, but the next reader of the docs viewer path is told the opposite of what the deployment now does.

samples.summary: Docs/comments outside the diff still say the share-link note surface has no view menu and does not use the per-browser note preferences
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-settings.ts:7`: "The owner editor (NotesDetail) reads them on open and writes them on change; the read-only shared viewer does not use them" — but `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-notes-layout.tsx:8-11,60-66` now seeds `viewMode`, `keymap` and `showAuthors` from exactly these readers. `docs/design/notes/notes.md:802-804` likewise still says the share-link page "has no menu" while the same doc's §248-272 describes the new toolbar, so the file now contradicts itself.

samples.summary: The share-token uploader is handed to the notes engine raw, so a failed image upload on an editor share link is reported to nobody
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-notes-layout.tsx:74` passes `shareTokenImageUploader(token)` — a `DocsImageUpload = (file) => Promise<string>` that **rejects** on failure (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/image-insert.ts:15,40-49`; `image-insert.test.ts:90` asserts it throws) — as the notes engine's `UploadImage`, whose contract is `Promise<string | null>` where `null` means "the host already reported this to the user" (`packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:18-26`). Every other consumer wraps it: the workspace note route toasts and returns `null` (`packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-detail.tsx:208-227`), and the docs share mount goes through `insertImageFromFile`'s try/catch + toast (`image-insert.ts:128-140`, used from `shared-document.tsx:332`). Here a rejection is only console-logged by the engine, so an anonymous editor's failed upload silently drops the placeholder with no UI feedback.

finding.summary: Flipping YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE to enforce-by-default activates a documented, unmitigated denial risk for existing deployments that already registered the webhook methods
finding.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:21) makes an unset variable mean *enforce*. The out-of-diff rollout contract this changes is recorded at docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:270-283: "A viewer ... client that still emits a local change on load ... → verb `rw` → the webhook denies it under enforcement. The React `DocumentProvider` does not currently expose a read-only/`syncMode` attach option, so this can't be forced from the frontend today. **Mitigation:** shadow mode is exactly the instrument for this — the rollout must confirm viewer-link attach/PushPull requests actually carry verb `r` (watch the shadow logs) before flipping ... =true." That mitigation is exactly what the new default removes: any deployment that already ran `--auth-webhook-method-add AttachDocument/PushPull` while relying on the shadow default (the state packages/backend/README.md:252-256 and docs/design/sharing.md:208 describe as the stock one) starts denying on upgrade, with no config change of its own, and the SDK-level fix the design doc names as the precondition is still a follow-up. Nothing in the diff addresses the migration for those installs; the only other consumers given a token were the backend's own clients.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. `isYorkieAuthEnforced` at packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:20-21 does make an unset YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE mean enforce (consumed at packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts:133-136), and the rollout contract the finding cites is present unchanged at docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:270-283, where the stated mitigation for the viewer/verb-`rw` denial risk is running shadow mode and confirming verb `r` "before flipping YORKIE_AUTH_WEBHOOK_ENFORCE=true", with the SDK read-only attach path listed as a follow-up. A default of enforce removes that precondition for any existing install that registered the webhook methods and configured nothing else. Corroborating out-of-diff consumers still state the old contract: docs/design/sharing.md:208-213 ("off by default ... stock deployment ... shadow mode"), packages/docs/src/store/read-only.ts:40, packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:4412-4414, packages/notes/src/store/read-only.ts:63-64. Two things I checked that could have refuted it did not: (a) packages/backend/README.md:252-256 has actually been updated to describe enforce-by-default, so that one citation is mischaracterized, but sharing.md:208 stands, and a single wrong citation does not make the finding not-present; (b) viewer attaches do avoid seeding a root (packages/frontend/src/app/shared/shared-document.tsx:974,992,1007,1020 via docsInitialRootForRole/notesInitialRootForRole/boardInitialRootForRole returning {} for viewer — packages/frontend/src/types/docs-document.ts:78, board-document.ts:26, notes-document.ts:67), which guards this app's known local-change-on-load vector but not the general risk the design doc records, and not the posture flip for an already-deployed install. No named refutation ground applies.
